notices.agenda_text:
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS and PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD
Eagle Mountain City, Utah
U.S. Housing and Urban Development (HUD)
Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Program
Preparation of Proposed Program Year (PY) 2026 HUD CDBG Annual Action Plan
Eagle Mountain City will hold a Public Hearing on Tuesday, August 4, 2026 during a regularly scheduled council meeting at 7:00 p.m. in Council Chambers, at City Hall at 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain City, Utah 84005.
This notice is provided in compliance with the City's adopted Citizen Participation Plan, as required by 24 CFR (Code of Federal Regulations) 91. The Eagle Mountain City Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) program is funded through the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).
Eagle Mountain City receives an annual allocation from the HUD CDBG program, as an Entitlement City. Eagle Mountain City (EMC) is preparing the required Program Year (PY) 2026 Annual Action Plan (AAP). The PY2026 allocation is currently estimated at $246,979, finalized with a grant agreement between EMC and HUD after HUD approval.
During the public hearing EMC staff, in accordance with HUD requirements, will outline goals and AAP projects under consideration for PY 2026 with CDBG funding.
Current funding outline includes:
Annual Allocation of $246,979 and Prior Year Resources of approximately $220,000, for a total of $466,979.
Project
Proposed Allocation
Housing Preservation and Development
$ 200,000
Public Services (capped at 15% of annual award)
$ 36,900
Public Facilities and Infrastructure Improvements
$ 180,879
PY 2026 Program Planning and Administration (capped at 20% of annual award)
$ 49,200
All amounts are estimates
The public is invited to attend this hearing and provide feedback on the EMC proposed AAP goals and projects.
NOTICE OF PUBLIC COMMENT PERIOD
A public comment period on the proposed Annual Action Plan will begin on July 1, 2026 at 10:00 am MDT. Public comment period will close on August 4, 2026 at 7:00 pm MDT.
Comments received by the City on or before the end of the comment period will be forwarded to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). Comments received after the comment period will not be considered.
A detailed account of the plans and activities associated with the CDBG program may be obtained by visiting the City's website at www.eaglemountain.gov, or by contacting Kiara Polee, Affordable Housing Coordinator, at telephone (801) 789-6700, or by email to kpolee@eaglemountain.gov.
Public notices regarding future public hearings for the 5-year Consolidated Plan, Annual Action Plans, and/or other HUD reports will be printed in a local newspaper of general circulation and posted online on the City's, website at www.eaglemountain.gov.
In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations should contact Taylor Draney at least five (5) days prior to the hearing. Individuals with hearing or speech impairments may dial 711 (Relay Utah).
Materials for public hearing items may be viewed within three days of the meeting on the city website and at the Eagle Mountain City Recorder's Office, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, UT, during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. If you need special accommodation to participate in the meeting, please call the City Recorder's Office at 801.789.6611. Open portions of the meeting can be viewed at www.eaglemountain.gov.
The undersigned, duly appointed City Recorder, does hereby certify that the above agenda notice was posted on this 19th day of June, 2026, on the Eagle Mountain City bulletin boards, the Eagle Mountain City website www.eaglemountain.gov, posted to the Utah State public notice website http://www.utah.gov/pmn/index.html, and was emailed to at least one newspaper of general circulation within the jurisdiction of the public body.
Lacie A. Messerly
City Recorder
THE PUBLIC IS INVITED TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.

CITY COUNCIL MEETING

JULY 7, 2026, 4:00 PM
EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS
1650 E STAGECOACH RUN, EAGLE MOUNTAIN, UT 84005

4:00 PM WORK SESSION - CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS

1.	DISCUSSION AND INFORMATION ITEMS
	This is an opportunity to provide information to the City Council. These items are for information only and do not require action by the City Council.

	1.A.	DISCUSSION - Legislative Update - Lobbyist, David Stewart
(anticipated time 15 minutes)

(anticipated time 20 minutes)

(anticipated time 10 minutes)

3.	AGENDA REVIEW
	The City Council will review items on the Consent Agenda and Policy Session Agenda.

4.	ADJOURN TO A CLOSED SESSION
	The City Council will adjourn into a Closed Session for the purpose of discussion of pending or reasonably imminent litigation; the character, professional competence, or physical or mental health of an individual; the purchase, lease, sale, or exchange of real property; a proposed development agreement, project proposal, or financing proposal related to the development of land owned by the state or a political subdivision; and/or the deployment of security personnel, devices, or systems, pursuant to Section 52-4-205(1) of the Utah Code, Annotated.


7:00 PM POLICY SESSION - CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS

9.	PROCLAMATIONS

	9.A.	PROCLAMATION - A Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming Eagle Mountain City as a Believer City.

10.	APPOINTMENTS

	10.A.	1.	Jessi Call - One Year appointment through May 31, 2027.
2.	Angeline Washburn - One Year appointment through May 31, 2027.

11.	PUBLIC COMMENTS
	Time has been set aside for the public to express their ideas, concerns, and comments. (Please limit your comments to three minutes each.)

12.	CITY COUNCIL/MAYOR ITEMS
	Time has been set aside for the City Council and Mayor to make comments.

CONSENT AGENDA

13.	BOND RELEASES

	13.A.	Parkway Fields Phase B, Plat 2 - Out of Warranty

14.	MINUTES

	14.A.	June 16, 2026 Minutes - Regular City Council Meeting

15.	RESOLUTIONS

	15.A.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement Renewal with Legislative Executive Consulting, LLC.

	15.B.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Medium Park in Overland Village 2 Phase B.

	15.C.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Water Tank Reimbursement Agreement with White Hills Water Company.

	15.D.	RESOLUTION - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Second Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

16.	ORDINANCES/PUBLIC HEARINGS

	16.A.	ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 17.64 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing an Alternative Energy Overlay Zone. 

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Director of Legislative and Strategic Affairs, Evan Berrett) Eagle Mountain City is proposing the creation of an overlay zone known as the Alternative Energy Overlay Zone (AEOZ) which would allow for the development of a variety of types of power generation facilities at approved locations. The AEOZ is not being proposed at this time to be applied to any property and would generally be contemplated for use on request. The AEOZ contains a number of requirements and restrictions regarding power generation facility development including demonstration of approval from state and federal entities as applicable.

	16.B.	ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions, 17.25.030 Land Use Table, and Enacting Chapter 17.44 Senior Housing Overlay Zone. 

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Housing Coordinator, Kiara Polee, and Long Range Planner, Elizabeth Fewkes) The City Council directed staff to create an overlay zone in an effort to encourage the construction of senior housing in the City.

	16.C.	ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.75.052 regarding Accessory Recreation Buildings.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Planner, Steven Lehmitz) A proposed code amendment that establishes special use standards for recreation buildings that are an accessory use to religious or cultural meeting halls.

	16.D.	ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions, Section 17.80.120, Political Signs and Section 17.80.160 Temporary Signs.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Planner, Steven Lehmitz) This proposed code amendment provides definitions for park strips and political signs, updates standards and practices for political signs, and updates standards for temporary and seasonal use signs.

	16.E.	ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Plan.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Community Development Director, Brandon Larsen) Eagle Mountain City is proposing an updated annexation policy plan. The plan identifies seven (7) areas of unincorporated Utah County that Eagle Mountain City would potentially consider for annexation. The document contains a map of these areas in relation to the current city boundaries. A series of criteria and considerations are included in the document to facilitate analysis and decision-making for annexation proposals.

17.	ORDINANCES

	17.A.	ORDINANCE - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Senior Planner, David Stroud) The City has had a number of instances in which Neighborhood Improvement has enforced residential parking codes, and they now ask the code be amended to better regulate parking standards. The proposed amendments are aimed at addressing issues related to the parking of unlicensed vehicles, trailers, etc. in a residential zone, as well as reducing the parking time limit on a public street.

18.	DISCUSSION/POSSIBLE ACTION

	18.A.	Discussion and Possible Action: Citywide Speed Management Study at Key Locations.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Assistant City Engineer David Salazar) Staff is seeking City Council direction regarding a proposed traffic study to evaluate identified roadway segments and intersections prior to implementation of future traffic calming measures. Council may provide direction regarding the study scope, locations to be analyzed, and authorization for staff to proceed with the study.

19.	LEGISLATIVE ITEMS

Please call the City Recorder's Office at least 3 working days prior to the meeting at 801-789-6611. This meeting may be held telephonically to allow a member of the public body to participate. This agenda is subject to change with a minimum 24-hour notice.

EAGLE MOUNTAIN CITY COUNCIL
NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS

The Eagle Mountain City Council will hold public hearings on June 16, 2026, at 7:00 PM or as soon thereafter as business allows, in the Eagle Mountain City Council Chambers, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, Utah 84005.  The City Council will receive public comments concerning the following items:


FY 2026-2027 Interim Budget Adoption:

-	FY 2026-2027 Interim Budget Adoption: Eagle Mountain City will hold a Public Hearing at 7:00 PM, on Tuesday, June 16, 2026, to accept public comment on the 2026-2027 fiscal year Interim Budget. The Public Hearing will be held at the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Building located at 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, in the City Council Chambers. Public comment is welcome. The proposed budget can be viewed at eaglemountain.gov/finance and in the office of the Eagle Mountain City Recorder. 

The Interim Budget will be in effect for the period beginning on July 1, 2026, and ending after August 18, 2026, upon the City Council's adoption of a final budget. The fiscal year 2026-2027 tentative budget presented to the City Council on May 5, 2026, proposes a property tax increase triggering the Truth-In-Taxation process. The Interim Budget sets aside, in a restricted budget account the additional property tax revenue generated by the proposed tax rate increase. The City may not expend or otherwise obligate the restricted revenue until the completion of the Truth-In-Taxation process and the City Council has taken action to adopt a final budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 subject to the requirements of Utah Code Section 52-2-919.  To view the property tax impact schedule and learn more about the proposed tax increase, visit eaglemountain.gov/truth-in-taxation-property-tax. 
EMC Point of Contact: Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch: kruesch@eaglemountain.gov.

-	Amendment #3 to the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Budget: The proposed budget amendment includes changes to the General Fund, Capital Project Fund, Special Revenue Funds, Internal Service Funds, and Enterprise Funds. EMC Point of Contact: Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch: kruesch@eaglemountain.gov. 

Compensation Increase: 

-	Executive Municipal Officers Compensation: Consideration of compensation increases for Executive Municipal Officers included in the proposed FY 2026-2027 Budget. EMC Point of Contact: Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch: kruesch@eaglemountain.gov.
Amendments to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code: 

-	EMMC Chapter 16.15: Consideration of an amendment to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.15 Concept Plans. EMC Point of Contact: Community Development Director, Brandon Larsen: blarsen@eaglemountain.gov.   
  

THE PUBLIC IS INVITED TO PARTICIPATE IN ALL CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS.

Materials for public hearing items may be viewed within three days of the meeting on the city website and at the Eagle Mountain City Recorder's Office, 1650 E Stagecoach Run, Eagle Mountain, UT, during normal business hours, Monday through Friday, 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM. If you need special accommodation to participate in the meeting, please call the City Recorder's Office at 801.789.6611.  Open portions of the meeting can be viewed at www.eaglemountain.gov. 

Certificate of Posting

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Director of Administrative Services, Kimberly Ruesch) State law requires the City to amend its budget to account for changes in expenditures. This resolution proposes the third amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Budget, incorporating previously approved Council actions, routine year-end accounting adjustments, and updates to Redevelopment Area revenues and expenditures based on actual activity.

	17.A.	PUBLIC HEARING ONLY - Pursuant to Utah Code 10-3-818(2)(b)(i), Consideration of Public Comment on Proposed Compensation Increases for Executive Officers in the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Budget.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Human Services Manager Angela Valenzuela) Cities are required to hold a public hearing separate from any other public hearing prior to adopting a final budget or a final amended budget that includes proposed compensation increases for executive municipal officers. Action on this item will be included with adoption of the FY2026-2027 Budget.

	17.B.	INFORMATION - Proposed Property Tax Impact Schedule 

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Mayor Jared Gray) As part of the Truth in Taxation process and in accordance with State requirements, the Mayor will read the Property Tax Impact Schedule during the meeting when the proposed budget is discussed. Members of the public will have an opportunity to appear and be heard regarding the proposed tax increase. The City Council will hold a public hearing regarding the proposed property tax increase on August 6, 2026, at 6:00 p.m. Members of the public will have an opportunity to appear and be heard regarding the proposed tax increase. For more information please go to: https://eaglemountain.gov/truth-in-taxation-property-tax/.

	17.C.	RESOLUTION/PUBLIC HEARING - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026-2027 Interim Budget and the Proposed Certified Tax Rate; and Discontinuing DebtBook Services.

BACKGROUND: (Presented by Administrative Services Director Kimberly Ruesch) State statute requires the City Council to hold a public hearing on the interim budget, conduct a Truth in Taxation public hearing scheduled for Thursday, August 6 at 6:00 PM, and adopt the final budget on August 18, 2026.

The City Council accepted the tentative budget on May 5, 2026, and set a Public Hearing on the interim budget for Tuesday, June 16, 2026 at 7:00 PM. An interim budget will be in effect from July 1, 2026, through August 18, 2026, or until the City Council adopts the final budget.

The final budget and certified tax rate will govern expenditures for Fiscal Year 2026-2027.
